evidence: All 23 custom agents use the `.agent` suffix; `AGENTS.md:23` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md:28` also document `.github/agents/*.agent`. Current GitHub custom-agent docs use `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md`.
risk: GitHub will not load the custom agent catalog, so the role system fails at the platform layer.
recommended_fix: Rename every file under `.github/agents/*.agent` to `.agent.md` and update every repo reference and validator glob to match.

evidence: `docs/agents/CANONICAL_ARTIFACT_POLICY.md:5-19` declares 6 required canonical files plus 5 supporting canonicals, while `AGENTS.md:12-16`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md:40-45`, and `.github/skills/swe-team-protocol/SKILL.md:39-49` center only 3 files.
risk: Different agents can legitimately believe different artifact sets are authoritative, which breaks handoffs and completion logic.
recommended_fix: Pick one canonical artifact contract and restate it consistently in `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, Team Lead, and `swe-team-protocol`.

evidence: `docs/agents/` is declared canonical, but `.github/docs/agents/` duplicates 24 artifacts and 11 have drift. Examples: `docs/agents/security-report.md` vs `.github/docs/agents/security-report.md`, `docs/agents/sre-report.md` vs `.github/docs/agents/sre-report.md`, `docs/agents/ux-review-report.md` vs `.github/docs/agents/ux-review-report.md`.
risk: Agents and humans can read or update the wrong copy, producing nondeterministic outputs and stale review evidence.
recommended_fix: Stop committing mutable mirrors, or regenerate `.github/docs/agents/` from the canonical tree only; never let both trees be editable.

evidence: `.github/agents/release-engineer.agent:53-75` writes `docs/agents/release-report.md` with JSON type `ReleasePlan`, while `.github/agents/release-manager.agent:121-184` writes the same file with JSON type `ReleaseReport`. `docs/agents/release-report.md:7` names `release-manager` as author, and `team-lead.agent:59-66` omits any release stage.
risk: The release artifact can be overwritten with incompatible schemas, and the release roles are not consistently reachable from the main manager workflow.
recommended_fix: Keep one release role and one JSON contract, update the Team Lead loop to invoke it explicitly, and delete or alias the other role.

evidence: `docs/agents/CANONICAL_ARTIFACT_POLICY.md:24-27` requires active-run artifacts under `docs/agents/runs/<run-id>/`, but `docs/agents/current-run.json` points to a run folder that lacks `patch-report.md`, `test-report.md`, and `release-report.md`. `.github/hooks/hooks.json:10-14,23-28,37-40,50-53,64-66` logs to shared `docs/agents/_hook-audit/*` instead of a run folder.
risk: Concurrent or repeated runs overwrite shared singleton files and lose run ownership, auditability, and reproducibility.
recommended_fix: Make `docs/agents/runs/<run-id>/` the owner for mutable artifacts and hook audit logs; keep only a pointer file at the root.

evidence: There are 111 stale `:contentReference[...]` markers across 19 files. Some corrupt content directly, e.g. `.github/skills/mcp-admin/SKILL.md:4,61` and `.github/agents/security-engineer.agent:118-122,149`.
risk: Agents read broken prose and malformed JSON examples, which increases prompt confusion and schema drift.
recommended_fix: Strip every `:contentReference[...]` marker and repair the damaged lines before using these prompts as canonical system instructions.

evidence: `.github/skills/team-lead/SKILL.md:20-22` tells the manager to start with `/swe-team-protocol`, but `.github/skills/team-lead/**` and `.github/skills/swe-team-protocol/**` duplicate the same schemas/templates with different content. Example differences: `templates/task-spec.template.md`, `templates/review-report.template.md`, and `templates/delegation/research-request.template.json`.
risk: The manager and protocol layers can generate different artifact shapes for the same handoff, which makes the system non-deterministic.
recommended_fix: Choose a single shared protocol package and make the other skill reference it instead of carrying divergent copies.

evidence: `docs/agents/review-report.md`, `docs/agents/patch-report.md`, `docs/agents/release-report.md`, many other report templates, and all `.github/agents/*.agent` files end with an opening ```json fence but no closing fence.
risk: Markdown rendering and copy/paste behavior become inconsistent, and schema examples are easier for models to misread.
recommended_fix: Close every fenced code block and add a validator that fails on odd fence counts in prompts and report templates.

evidence: `scripts/ci/check_agent_system.py:29-32,66-72` validates `.github/agents/*.agent` and checks `.github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.md`, then reports PASS. It does not validate the real `.yml` workflow path, official `.agent.md` naming, mirror drift, release-role collisions, or malformed markdown fences.
risk: The repo reports a clean agent system while critical compatibility and determinism issues remain undetected.
recommended_fix: Retarget the validator to the official GitHub paths and add checks for mirror drift, duplicate artifact owners, fence balance, and run-scoped artifact policy.

evidence: `.github/hooks/hooks.json` executes `scripts/hooks/*`, while `.github/scripts/hooks/*` contains wrapper duplicates that forward to the root scripts. The repo therefore has two hook-script roots for the same behavior.
risk: Future changes can update one hook root and not the other, creating silent drift and review confusion.
recommended_fix: Keep one hook script root only; because hooks.json already points at `scripts/hooks/*`, either delete `.github/scripts/hooks/*` or regenerate it from the canonical root.
